intro: At inference, batch normalization uses fixed running statistics. Combine it with a preceding affine layer to produce exactly the same outputs with one affine operation.
task: Return folded weights and bias for batch normalization applied to x@weights+bias.
signature: fold_batchnorm(weights, bias, mean, variance, gamma, beta, epsilon)
requirements: weights has shape input-by-output. All five vectors bias, mean, variance, gamma, beta have output width. variance is nonnegative and epsilon is in [1e-8,1].
Let scale=gamma/sqrt(variance+epsilon). Return {"weights": weights*scale across columns, "bias": (bias-mean)*scale+beta}. Use fixed evaluation statistics, not current batch statistics.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Two output scales
examples.output:
{'weights': [[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]], 'bias': [1.0, 2.0]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Zero gamma
examples.output:
{'weights': [[0.0]], 'bias': [7.0]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Negative gamma
examples.output:
{'weights': [[-1.0]], 'bias': [1.0]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Each output column has its own normalization scale.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: The original bias participates before subtracting the running mean.

explanation: Fixed normalization is an affine transform, so composing it with a linear layer gives another affine transform. Folding avoids a separate normalization operation during evaluation.
The equivalence depends on fixed statistics. Recomputing mean and variance from each input batch would make the transform input-dependent and would not permit this same fold.
